pins.name: Berry Patch Trailhead (Trail #95, connects to Trail #96)
pins.evidence: Four of the recorded round trips (including the chosen NW Ridge one) start here, at about 4,650 ft. WTA and the Forest Service describe Berry Patch as a separate trailhead on FR-2150 near Chambers Lake, a short distance past the Snowgrass turnoff, with a connector to Trail 96; OSM maps it 300 m from Chambers Lake Campground, which matches. Our existing Snowgrass Flats pin matches WTA's stated coordinate (46.4642, -121.5190), so it stays.
pins.confirmedBy: https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search?format=json&q=Berry+Patch+Trailhead+Washington (OSM trailhead node); name and location relation also from https://www.fs.usda.gov/r06/giffordpinchot/recreation/berry-patch-trailhead and WTA's Snowgrass hike page

facts.text: Day hikers above the summit block can knock loose stones onto the scramble below (late July)
A high camp near the PCT meadows around 6,500 ft beside a small stream puts the summit about 1.4 miles and 1,100 ft away; the upper end of the meadows has fewer mosquitoes.
After leaving US-12 the approach road is about 16 miles of unpaved washboard; no big potholes in late August, but higher clearance is more comfortable.
By mid-September only small snow patches sit near the summit and the scramble is straightforward class 2 talus with decent footing.
In early October the route was completely free of snow, with the berry bushes at peak colour in the meadows.
